newsitem.title: USA: Former Doris Duke butler found dead.
newsitem.headline: Former Doris Duke butler found dead.

text.p: Bernard Lafferty, the former butler to Doris Duke who was recently cleared of allegations that he plotted to murder the tobacco heiress, was found dead at his home Monday, officials said.

Lafferty, who was 51, was discovered "lifeless in bed" in his home in the posh suburb of Bel Air and appeared to have died of natural causes, said Scott Carrier, a spokesman for the Los Angeles County coroner's office.

Carrier said an investigation was under way to rule out foul play, although the circumstances of his death were not suspicious. Lafferty was known to be under the treatment of a doctor for an unknown medical condition, Carrier said.

Lafferty became embroiled in a high-profile battle over Duke's $1.2 billion estate when a nurse who had worked for the heiress claimed Lafferty had helped one of Duke's doctors administer her a lethal dose of morphine. Both men denied the allegation.
Duke, the only child of American Tobacco Co. founder James Buchanan, was 80 at the time of her death in 1993 and named Lafferty the executor of her estate.

But the allegations against Lafferty and the doctor unravelled after the nurse, Tammy Payette, was found pawning jewelry and other valuables from the home of Duke and other wealthy patients who employed her. Payette is currently serving an eight-year prison sentence for theft.

In May, a New York judge approved a plan to send the bulk of Duke's estate to charity, and removed Lafferty as co-executor in return for a $4.5 million lump-sum payment and another $500,000 a year for life.
In July, the Los Angeles district attorney's office said an investigation into Duke's death concluded there was "no credible evidence" that she was murdered.
